parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · Fraser Valley Regional District Electoral Area C, tagged Mission in MLS® · Highway 7, FVRD Area C

Lake Errock is a sub-area in the MLS® system, and the Fraser Valley Regional District does not publish a boundary for it. It lies in the Fraser Valley Regional District, not within the City of Mission.
Area C’s plan area stretches east from the Harrison River past Deroche, taking in Lake Errock, Harrison Mills, Morris Valley and the eastern parts of the Deroche Bench.
The FVRD page places Lake Errock on Highway 7 (Lougheed Highway) between Mission and Agassiz.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the Fraser Valley Regional District and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).

parts.t: Adopted
The FVRD’s Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 1747, 2024, was adopted at the Board meeting on September 18, 2025, and includes dedicated Neighbourhood Plans for Harrison Mills and Lake Errock
Revision
On June 25, 2026 the FVRD Board adopted Revision Bylaw No. 1841, 2026, which updated the plan’s minimum parcel size table (policy 3.12.10) and its development permit exemptions (policy 12.1.2)
Area
The Area C plan area spans from the Harrison River to east of Deroche and includes Morris Valley, Harrison Mills, Lake Errock and the eastern portions of the Deroche Bench

Planning, zoning and flood

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Lake Errock

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The eastern portions of the Deroche Bench, Lake Errock, Harrison Mills and Morris Valley are all inside the Area C plan area, which runs from the Harrison River to a point east of Deroche.
The FVRD’s Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 1747, 2024, was adopted at the Board meeting on September 18, 2025, and includes dedicated Neighbourhood Plans for Harrison Mills and Lake Errock.
On June 25, 2026 the FVRD Board adopted Revision Bylaw No. 1841, 2026, which updated the plan’s minimum parcel size table (policy 3.12.10) and its development permit exemptions (policy 12.1.2).
The FVRD page says the public hearing on the Area C plan was held on August 12, 2025.

A developer applied to redevelop the former gravel pit at 43837 and 43873 Lougheed Highway (called Harrison Rise) into a subdivision of about 485 dwelling units, in a mix of single-family lots, townhouses, apartments and multiplexes. The FVRD page says the developer withdrew its zoning amendment application on March 7, 2025, to pursue an Official Community Plan amendment.
The FVRD’s servicing feasibility work found the community water part of Harrison Rise financially viable, while the new community sewer needed would have significant cost challenges.
The FVRD page says under the previous plan most of the gravel pit lands were designated Limited Use, which supports low-density development on 8-hectare parcels.
The FVRD’s Area C project page says BC Transit and the FVRD held a survey and open houses on a possible “North of Fraser Transit” service, and that the consultation has concluded.
I found no area-specific floodplain or geohazard detail for Lake Errock on the pages I read, so check the plan’s development permit areas with the FVRD.
BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley list has no route naming Lake Errock. For Mission it shows 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 39.

FAQ
Where is Lake Errock?
Lake Errock is an MLS® sub-area name. The Fraser Valley Regional District doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
Covering the area from the Harrison River eastward beyond Deroche, the Area C plan area also takes in the Deroche Bench’s eastern portions, along with Lake Errock, Harrison Mills and Morris Valley.
How do I get around from Lake Errock?
The Central Fraser Valley route list at BC Transit covers 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 and 39 for Mission, and Lake Errock is not named on any route.
BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley list also includes 66 Fraser Valley Express, 71 Agassiz-Harrison and 72 Hope.
The FVRD’s Area C project page says BC Transit and the FVRD held a survey and open houses on a possible “North of Fraser Transit” service, and that the consultation has concluded.
The nearest West Coast Express station is Mission City Station, at 33200 North Railway Avenue in Mission.
Which schools are near Lake Errock?
I found no school in Lake Errock. Deroche Elementary, Kindergarten to 6, is at 10340 N Deroche Rd.
SD75’s catchment policy puts Deroche Elementary in the Hatzic Middle School catchment.
Catchments are set by address, so confirm a specific address with
Mission Public Schools (School District 75)
, which publishes a catchment map.
What libraries and parks are there?
The nearest libraries are the Agassiz Library at 7140 Cheam Avenue and the Mission Library at 33247 Second Avenue.
I found no FVRD park or boat launch listing for Lake Errock on the pages I read.
What plan covers Lake Errock?
The FVRD’s Area C Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 1747, 2024, was adopted at the Board meeting on September 18, 2025, and includes dedicated Neighbourhood Plans for Harrison Mills and Lake Errock.
On June 25, 2026 the FVRD Board adopted Revision Bylaw No. 1841, 2026, which updated the plan’s minimum parcel size table (policy 3.12.10) and its development permit exemptions (policy 12.1.2).
